source.author: stat
source.text: discurrunt muris; nil saeptum horrore sub illo, nil fidum satis, invalidaeque Amphionis arces, rumor ubique alios pluresque adnuntiat hostes maioresque timor; spectant tentoria contra Inachia externosque suis in montibus ignes, hi precibus questuque deos, hi Martia tela belligerosque hortantur equos, hi pectora fletu cara premunt miserique rogos et crastina mandant funera, si tenuis demisit lumina somnus, bella gerunt; modo lucra morae, modo taedia vitae attonitis, lucemque timent lucemque precantur.
source.text_original: discurrunt muris; nil saeptum horrore sub illo, / nil fidum satis, invalidaeque Amphionis arces, / rumor ubique alios pluresque adnuntiat hostes / maioresque timor; spectant tentoria contra / Inachia externosque suis in montibus ignes, / hi precibus questuque deos, hi Martia tela / belligerosque hortantur equos, hi pectora fletu / cara premunt miserique rogos et crastina mandant / funera, si tenuis demisit lumina somnus, / bella gerunt; modo lucra morae, modo taedia vitae / attonitis, lucemque timent lucemque precantur.
source.text_english: They rush about the walls; under that terror nothing is securely enclosed, nothing sufficiently safe, and the citadels of Amphion are weak. Rumor everywhere announces other, more numerous enemies, and fear still greater ones; they look across at the tents of Inachus, and at foreign fires on their own mountains. Some with prayers and lamentation implore the gods, some urge on warlike weapons and war-loving horses, some press dear ones to their breasts with tears and, wretched, make arrangements for pyres and next-day funerals if sleep has let their eyes fall closed. They wage war; for some, delay is gain, for others, in their panic, life’s weariness. They fear the light and pray for the light.

reuse.text: discurrunt transtris: hi celso cornua malo expediunt, alii tonsas in marmore summo praetemptant, prora funem legit Argus ab alta.
reuse.text_original: discurrunt transtris: hi celso cornua malo / expediunt, alii tonsas in marmore summo / praetemptant, prora funem legit Argus ab alta.
reuse.text_english: They run about on the benches: some clear the yardarms from the tall mast, others try the oars upon the high marble, and from the lofty prow Argus gathers in the rope.
